name: Blank Bio
long_description:
Blank Bio is an applied AI research lab focused on increasing the success rates of clinical trials. We do this by training RNA foundation models that learn the patterns that shape disease progression and patient response to treatment. We aim to help pharma make more informed decisions in clinical trials by capturing the biology that makes each patient’s tumour unique. 

We’re a technical team of AI scientists and engineers from companies including Recursion, Deep Genomics, DeepMind, and Amazon, and institutions including Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Centre, Stanford, and the Vector Institute.

launches.title: Blank Bio - Biological AI Models to Predict Patient Outcomes
launches.tagline: We predict patient survival and treatment response to increase clinical trial success
launches.body:
**TL;DR:**

Today, we are excited to introduce [Ladon](https://www.blank.bio/introducing-ladon), a state-of-the-art RNA foundation model that predicts disease trajectory and treatment response in patients. There is immense complexity in the individual biology of every patient. Two patients can have the same diagnosis and receive the same treatment, yet have very different outcomes: one responds well and lives for years, while the other’s disease continues to progress. Understanding and resolving this heterogeneity to predict outcomes is how we unlock clinical trial abundance and ultimately accelerate our delivery of medicines for patients. Ladon is our first step towards this future: one where we can learn more from every patient enrolled so that we can run smaller, faster trials with higher success rates. We built it to give drug developers quantitative support on billion-dollar clinical trial decisions.

**Ask:** Do you know someone in clinical development or translational medicine at a pharma or biotech? We’d love an introduction. Please email us at [founders@blank.bio](mailto:founders@blank.bio)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128643&key=user_uploads/1842799/7216db80-e659-487b-8cb8-d478539fbff6)

— 

### The Problem

Drugs are getting easier to design, but the bottleneck is still the clinic: 95% of cancer drugs that enter clinical trials never get approved. With more therapies to test than ever before, clinical trial decisions become harder and harder. This is in large part due to patient heterogeneity. Two patients can have the same diagnosis and receive the same treatment, yet have very different outcomes: one responds well and lives for years, while the other’s disease continues to progress. Fundamentally, the challenge with making clinical trial decisions is that we don’t have good enough tools to reliably predict therapeutic response and patient prognosis.

### Our solution

* Ladon is a 3B parameter model trained on millions of RNA-seq samples that span decades of data across labs, sequencing machines, cell lines, animal models, humans, and more.
* We are state-of-the-art, beating gene expression baselines, established biomarkers, and existing RNA foundation models at predicting patient prognosis and therapeutic response in various settings spanning 120+ oncology tasks, including external validation on 8 retrospectively analyzed clinical trials.
* More importantly, we demonstrate that Ladon-derived predictions are also robust and generalize across tissue and clinical trial cohorts. In the technical report, you’ll see that every evaluation is measured in an out-of-distribution setting like a held-out clinical trial, another cohort, or another measurement platform.
* We’ve built it with interpretability in mind. We also show that Ladon is best-in-class at inferring cell composition of bulk RNA-seq samples to make insights actionable.

### For pharma and diagnostic companies

All Ladon needs is RNA-seq from tumor samples. If you have banked samples, **we will pay for the RNA-sequencing costs!** Here are some potential applications:

* **Help with go / no-go decision making:** will a Phase 2 response turn into a survival benefit in Phase 3?
* **Contextualize single-arm trial results**: build synthetic control arms to see how patients would’ve done on standard of care
* **End trials earlier:** adjusting for prognostic signal at baseline can increase trial efficiency and end trials months earlier. Get to market faster!
* **Develop novel signatures:** find prognostic and predictive signal that actually hold up in the real world. We can also show that your biomarker is truly predictive by adjusting for prognostic baselines

### Our ask

* Please [reach out](https://www.blank.bio/contact) to us if you’d like to get access to the model
* You can read our [blog](https://www.blank.bio/introducing-ladon) and [technical report](https://www.blank.bio/ladon-technical-report) for more technical details
* If you know any clinical development or translational leaders across pharma or biotech, we’d love to get an intro

<https://youtu.be/fIS6qyKh7L8>

launches.title: Blank Bio - Computational toolkit for RNA therapeutics
launches.tagline: Building foundation models to design better RNA therapeutics, starting with mRNA design.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Jonny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jonathanhsuuw/), [Ian](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ruian-shi-4b5215b9/), and [Phil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/philip-fradkin-330a417b/), co-founders of [Blank Bio](https://www.blank.bio/) 👋

We’ve spent decades applying machine learning to biology across academia (Ph.D.’s at the University of Toronto) and industry (Recursion, Deep Genomics, Amazon). 

https://youtu.be/7lULj-S-MgQ?feature=shared

**TLDR:** 

* mRNA enables programmable, personalized medicine, from gene therapies to cancer vaccines. But with more possible sequences than stars in the universe, brute-force design is impossible.
* We built a state-of-the-art RNA foundation [model](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.10.10.617658v3) to predict and design high-performing sequences, letting pharma **simulate costly experiments** and speed up timelines. 
* Our open-source models are used by Sanofi and GSK, and we’re working with the Arc Institute to power next-gen virtual cell models.
* mRNA design is just the beginning. We’re expanding to applications like target identification, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and more

**Asks:** We’re looking to connect with pharma and biotech companies working on mRNA-based therapeutics (i.e. Moderna, BioNTech, Orbital etc.), CRISPR therapeutics (Scribe, Intellia, Editas, etc.), and biomarker discovery.

📤If you know anyone in those spaces, we’d love an intro: [jonathan@blank.bio](mailto:jonathan@blank.bio) 📤

**Who are we?**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92787&key=user_uploads/1842799/964fb41d-c751-418d-aecb-5dbbd0fc7405)

* **Jonny**: One of the first employees at Valence Discovery, an AI for drug discovery company spun out of Mila. Acquired by Recursion (NASDAQ: RXRX). Biochemist by training (Waterloo) 
* **Ian**: 10 years of experience in comp bio. Prev. researcher at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Centre (now leading the charge on cancer vaccines) and engineer at Amazon. Has a PhD in computer science (University of Toronto)
* **Phil**: 12 years of experience in ML for bio. Spent 4 years at Deep Genomics, where he was one of the first employees. Has a PhD in computational biology (University of Toronto)

Phil and Jonny previously worked together at Recursion. Ian and Phil have been collaborating for 5 years throughout their PhDs, doing ML research specifically for RNA biology. See preprints on early versions of the [model](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.10.10.617658v3) + [benchmark](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.07.05.662870v1). 

**What’s the problem?** 

mRNA is composed of four nucleotides (A, C, G, U). For the average mRNA therapeutic, there are \~10²⁷⁰⁹ possible combinations. This is unimaginably larger than the number of stars that exist in the known universe. 

A suboptimal sequence can kill your drug discovery program, costing pharma companies billions of dollars. But testing all of the possible sequences is impossible. How can you design the best sequence? 

**What are we building?** 

A family of RNA-specific foundation models that simulate costly and time-consuming experiments, predicting key properties like **expression** (how much protein is made from the mRNA) and **stability** (how long it stays in the body) before experiments ever begin. 

We’ve currently got the best **RNA foundation model**. It’s outperforming 59 models from leading research labs and companies. At 10M parameters, it’s lightweight and fast enough to run predictions on hundreds of sequences in seconds. The open-source model is already being used by **Sanofi and GSK**, and we’re also collaborating with the **Arc Institute** to bring our RNA embeddings into the next generation of virtual cells. 

**What’s next?** 

* We’re establishing a set of scaling laws that will bring a GPT-3 moment to RNA.  
* We’re curating one of the largest transcriptomic annotation datasets in the world to power model training
* As we improve the model, we’re expanding beyond mRNA design into a broader RNA toolkit, tackling problems like:
  * Target ID
  * Novel biomarker discovery 
  * Cell-type-specific mRNA design
  * …and more 👀

Here’s a peek into the vision that we’re building towards.

https://youtu.be/ZgI7WJ1SygI

**Our Ask**

* Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/blank-bio) and[ X](https://x.com/blankbio_) 
* Share this post! 
* We’re looking to connect with pharma and biotech companies working on mRNA-based therapeutics (i.e. Moderna, BioNTech, Orbital, etc.), CRISPR therapeutics (Scribe, Intellia, Editas, etc.), and RNA biomarkers. An intro to anyone at these types of organizations would be huge. Please drop an email to [jonathan@blank.bio](mailto:jonathan@blank.bio)
